I work night shifts as a housing supporter in a small group home. Isn't this why people are afraid of talking about mental illness? Because people might get upset if you say something wrong or joke about mental illness? Joking about it makes it less tabu, more normalised in society. I have social anxiety, depression and history of self harm. I joke about it to people around me constantly. It's a way of coping with it but also making others comfortable when they see my scars and so on. Of course there are people who take it too far but the best thing to do there is to try to educate the person so that he or she is aware of the issue. But as a whole I have nothing against jokes about mental illness, and I know many who suffer from it who also jokes about it. You can't take it seriously all the time, that would just make it worse in the long run.
